The latest dev branch should work.
```console
% uvx --refresh git+https://gitlab.com/Chips4Makers/c4m-arrakeen-memgen.git@dev
This is project Arrakeen's memory generator.
This is pre-alpha quality software; just above proof-of-concept level.
Don't use it for production; no support is provided and use is at own risk!
If it breaks you may keep the pieces.

Select technologies:
1) IHP SG13G2
2) Sky130
3) GF180MCU

...```
512 is max. number of words currently supported by the compiler. The decoder generation for bigger number of words is not implemented yet.

I'm gonna draw up a 2L flex board using the JLC special (5pcs up to 100x100 2L 1/3oz thin PI core only no stiffeners no soldering); I'm currently planning to do a multi-opportunity breakout board that utilizes the 3 flip chip bond pad structures in various combinations/styles (there's 3 nets; 2 of the 3 structures only have one pad per net; the third structure has larger grid pads and offers each net twice and routed so that it's at most diagonally/corner adjacent not sidways to challenge bonding processes that may be prone to shorting out adjacent pins), wiring out the DUT nets to some sort of "connector" that an ohmmeter can then be connected to for testing bond quality.
What kind of connector would you think I should go with there?
Some kinda 4-wire ZIF style replicated around the outer border to hopefully cover all the DUT bonds so that a tester could be ZIF-connected to all of them in series to try them?
Just a wider ZIF connector for like each DUT/bond site approximately and plan on using an external breakout from that to a pin header or such?
Solder connections for attaching pin headers to the flex around the edge after the flip chip bonding has been done?

Any opinions? @Essen @Lauri @Andrew Wingate ?

Primary testing would be 4-wire measurements of nets through the bonds at both ends; where applicable isolation testing is also on the docket.
Where there are more than 2 pads for each net bonded out (there are 4 pads on the die for each net, but most DUT bonding sites on the test flex won't have all of them), the results from pairwise 4-wire measurements ought to reveal per-bond resistance, though possibly it might require adding a third voltage measurement wire into it, I'm not sure off the top of my head.

yeah works.

I took a look at the decoder generation code and it seems `RowPreDecodersT` could be taught to handle `(address_groups[0] != 3)`, specifically, `(address_groups[0] == 4)`, for a straight forward one extra bit (so up to 1024 words), as well as an easy extension by allowing to layer another pre-decoder in front of the current pre-decoder, where the new pre-decoder would merely act on this new (optional) 4th input bit of the current pre-decoder stage.
It'd have to spread them a bit more vertically I think to not get routing congestion at the current last level decoder/page pitch, but otherwise I think it should work? And like, without having to make the row periphery wider. Unless this would not possibly fit in the limited routing channels on the left side over the input DFFs; it does look quite tight there. On further look it does appear to be mighty tight already....
Seems like it'd still be worth it though, at least with a word size notably larger than the tiny 8 bit (so that the extra decoder column of row periphery space doesn't dominate).

I doubt I’ll be able to insert diodes inside the RAM, so I hope that’ll be enough.
Ideally you wouldn't be editing the GDS but wrapping it.

Ideally OpenROAD should be able to handle the SRAM as is and do proper supply connection and antenna diode insertion.
@Tholin Are you using librelane ? For my tape-outs @Leo Moser (mole99) helped me doing the tape-outs without needing to wrap the memory block. If I remember correctly for the half slot test chip the blocks were rotated also. It did contain minimal amount of logic though.

Idk how the Metal5 power straps could possibly connect to the RAM if it has no rails on Metal4
And indeed the PDN did not make any connections until I added those
But right now I’m more concerned about the antenna violations
pdn gen is perfectly capable to connect down from Met5 to lower metal, adding island and via stacks as needed.
But that's not something it will just do with default config.
The generated LEF file is missing antenna information, maybe that’s why librelane is struggling to pick up on the antenna violations.
Under normal circumstances, I’d do a LEF write from magic and have it generate this data, but it still gets stuck in an infinite loop when I try.

I’m more concerned with the antenna errors

messages.content: but no information on planarity requirement? does it list the sphere size?

not directly, at least without "inquiry".
As for planarity, well, it's generally a complex topic, due to how it interacts when manufacturing stuff.

I had found a paper that did a test die they plated copper pillars onto and pushed face bonding rectangular array pad pitch substantially beyond what we could reasonably hope for on our stuff, at least without finding an MPW source for cheap silicon interposers or doing cursed stuff with face-to-face bonding of gf180mcuD dies (imagine face-bonding a half-height slot stuffed with SRAM and not having a bond pad ring, right over the core area of a full slot that otherwise gets "regular" COB wire bonding, to attach a comfy amount of fast RAM (_very_ many pins possible, and no need for remotely bulky drivers due to inherently small capacitances) to something like a "normal" microcontroller or other general purpose ASIC).

Edit: yeah, like maybe 128 kiB or a bit less could probably fit, I guess...
I'll have to get outside and take care of some stuff while places are still open, and will see to grab the paper and whatever ACF nuances it iirc mentioned/detailed when I'm back home.

@azonenberg here, the paper:
they did 55μm pitch with the following:
>>> The bumps obtained were 6 µm high above the pad, with a diameter of 19 µm.
For the flip-chip hybridisation, an ACF of 18 µm thickness containing 3 µm-diameter nickel-
coated conductive particles (CP) with a density of 71,200 CP/mm² was used. The ACF was
laminated on the Ti-LGAD sensors at 90 °C under a pressure of 3.2 kgf (Fig. 1b), followed by
bonding at 160 °C under 20 kgf for 2 s using a SET ACCµRA100 flip-chip bonder [7].

Excluding the weak center they attribute to vacuum grooves in the bonder head used (they could have done without the grooves but didn't have such a head ready/on hand), they got 99.5% well-connected bonds
(for the record, we're aiming at like 30μm x 30μm pads at the small end, not 19μm diameter circles)
